# COR001 `implicit-typing`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A module, program or external procedure has no `implicit none`.

## Why

Without `implicit none` an undeclared or misspelled name silently becomes a new variable typed by
its first letter (`i`-`n` integer, otherwise real). The program compiles and computes with garbage.
`implicit none` in a module or program also covers every procedure they contain. An `implicit`
statement mapping letters to types is reported too: it keeps implicit typing alive.

## Reported

```fortran
module solver
contains
  subroutine step(n)
    integer, intent(in) :: n
    itr = n + 1   ! typo of 'iter': a new implicit integer
  end subroutine step
end module solver
```

## Preferred

```fortran
module solver
implicit none
...
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[COR001] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = COR001` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).
